statement: The organization table of the Army of the Potomac lists, under the general headquarters of the Second Army Corps, the 6th New York Cavalry, Companies D and K, Capt. Riley Johnson.

source.author: Organization of the Army of the Potomac, Maj. Gen. George G. Meade, commanding, at the battle of Gettysburg, July 1-3, 1863
source.page_basis: scan-leaf map docs/battle-theatre/kit/evidence/or27_leaf_pages.json, part 1, leaf 180, printed page 157 (the running heads inside the table are not all legible)
source.quote: 6th New York Cavalry, Companies D and K, Capt. Riley Johnson
source.cite: OR Ser. I vol. 27 pt. 1, OR27-1-R009 Organization of the Army of the Potomac, Maj. Gen. George G. Meade, commanding, at the battle of Gettysburg, July 1-3, 1863, p. 157

unit.name: 6th New York Cavalry, Companies D and K (II Corps headquarters)

note: Hancock (R076) and Caldwell (R077) name orderlies of Company D, 6th New York Cavalry: see the records of the headquarters company. The table prints no figure for the two companies.

statement: A footnote of the organization table, to the entry of Battery B, 1st New York Light Artillery, in Hazard's Artillery Brigade, prints that the battery was transferred from the Artillery Reserve on 1 July and that the 14th New York Battery was attached to it.

source.author: Organization of the Army of the Potomac, Maj. Gen. George G. Meade, commanding, at the battle of Gettysburg, July 1-3, 1863
source.page_basis: scan-leaf map docs/battle-theatre/kit/evidence/or27_leaf_pages.json, part 1, leaf 182, printed page 159 (the running heads inside the table are not all legible)
source.quote: Transferred from ArtiQery Reserve, July 1; 14th New York Battery attached.
source.cite: OR Ser. I vol. 27 pt. 1, OR27-1-R009 Organization of the Army of the Potomac, Maj. Gen. George G. Meade, commanding, at the battle of Gettysburg, July 1-3, 1863, p. 159

unit.name: 14th New York Battery (attached to Battery B, 1st New York Light Artillery)

note: The plan's order of battle has no entry of its own for the 14th New York Battery. The OCR prints ArtiQery for Artillery. Hazard (R132) calls the battery "Battery B, First New York Artillery" throughout.

statement: The narrative of the New York commission says that to Battery B, 1st New York Light Artillery, better known as Pettit's battery, the Fourteenth New York Independent Battery had been attached, and that Captain Rorty of the latter commanded both, assigned the day before 3 July.
reasoning: The narrative of the New York commission is a later compilation; it agrees with the organization table that the 14th New York battery was attached to Battery B, 1st New York Light Artillery, and adds that Captain Rorty of the 14th commanded both.

source.author: the narrative of the New York monuments commission in New York at Gettysburg, volume 1
source.quote: To this command had been attached the Fourteenth New York Independent Battery.
source.cite: New York at Gettysburg (1900) vol. 1, the narrative of the New York monuments commission in New York at Gettysburg, volume 1, section NY1-S001, p. 81~82

statement: The dedication address of Battery B, 1st New York Light Artillery (Pettit's battery), says that in 1863 a small addition of tried soldiers was made to the battery from the Fourteenth New York Battery.
reasoning: The address is a later speech at the dedication of the monument of Battery B; it says Battery B received men of the Fourteenth New York Battery in 1863, which agrees with the footnote of the organization table (attached, not merged into a battery of its own).

source.author: address of Rev. W. O. Beauchamp at the dedication of the monument of Battery B, 1st New York Light Artillery, 3 July 1888
source.quote: A small addition of brave and tried soldiers was made from the Fourteenth New York Battery in 1863
source.cite: New York at Gettysburg (1902) vol. 3, address of Rev. W. O. Beauchamp at the dedication of the monument of Battery B, 1st New York Light Artillery, 3 July 1888, section NY3-S022, p. 1169~1178

statement: Hancock prints that the Second Corps arrived on the field about 7 a. m. on 2 July, after resuming the march at daylight from the bivouac 3 miles in rear of the town, and was soon placed in position along the crest from the left of Cemetery Hill to Round Top Mountain.
reasoning: Hancock prints the hour of the corps' arrival on the field and the line it was placed in, along the crest from the left of Cemetery Hill to Round Top Mountain; Meade (R006) calls the position he and Howard posted the troops on the Cemetery Ridge, the gazetteer ridge GZ-006.

source.author: Maj. Gen. Winfield S. Hancock
source.quote: arrival on the field, which took place about 7 a. m. of the 2d
source.cite: OR Ser. I vol. 27 pt. 1, OR27-1-R076 Maj. Gen. Winfield S. Hancock, p. 369

place.printed: the crest from the left of Cemetery Hill to Round Top Mountain

note: The ledger holds this passage as an arrival_road claim without a road (POS-B-us-2c-09). The gate of the corps in arrivals.json also carries 22:30 on 1 July, about 06:00 and dawn: those values come from sources the plan marks weak or from a regimental history, and are not repeated here.

statement: A dispatch of 6.15 a. m. on 2 July from Meade's adjutant-general, S. Williams, to the chief of staff reports that the Second Corps is up and the Fifth is momentarily expected.

source.author: S. Williams, Assistant Adjutant-General
source.quote: The Second Corps is up and the Fifth is momentarily expected.
source.cite: OR Ser. I vol. 27 pt. 3, OR27-3-D2099 S. Williams, Assistant Adjutant-General, p. ~1086 (1086-1087)

note: The OCR prints the year 18G3. "Up" in the usage of the dispatch means come up to the army on the field; the passage prints no place of the corps. The hour is the hour of writing, not of the arrival: the corps was up before it.

statement: Hancock prints that on the morning of 2 July the Third Division (Hays) was placed on the right of the corps line, the Second Division (Gibbon) in the center and the First Division (Caldwell) on the left.

source.author: Maj. Gen. Winfield S. Hancock
source.quote: Brigadier-General Hays commanding, was placed on the right; the Second Division,
source.cite: OR Ser. I vol. 27 pt. 1, OR27-1-R076 Maj. Gen. Winfield S. Hancock, p. 369

note: Gibbon (R098) prints the same order of the divisions.

statement: Hancock prints that the strength of the corps in the action was about 10,000 officers and men and that its losses were 4,323 killed, wounded and missing.

source.author: Maj. Gen. Winfield S. Hancock
source.quote: The strength of the corps in the action was about 10,000 officers and men.
source.cite: OR Ser. I vol. 27 pt. 1, OR27-1-R076 Maj. Gen. Winfield S. Hancock, p. 375

note: The figure is for the action of 2 and 3 July; the date given is the day of the Wheatfield. The return of 30 June (R008) prints 968 officers and 12,088 men present for duty for the corps under Hancock (kit evidence us-2c-1d:0139).

statement: Hancock names the corps' march of 1 July by its two ends, Taneytown and Gettysburg; the road between those two places is the Taneytown Road of the gazetteer.
reasoning: The road is named by its two ends, Taneytown and Gettysburg (the form the road concordance resolves to the Taneytown Road, GZ-042); Hazard (R132), whose brigade moved with the corps, prints the Taneytown road for the same night and march.

source.author: Maj. Gen. Winfield S. Hancock
source.quote: marched from Taneytown toward Gettysburg at 1..30 p. m.
source.cite: OR Ser. I vol. 27 pt. 1, OR27-1-R076 Maj. Gen. Winfield S. Hancock, p. 369

road_identification.basis: The march is printed by its two ends, Taneytown and Gettysburg, and Hazard (R132) prints the Taneytown road for the artillery brigade that moved with the corps on that march, to a position 3 miles southeast of Gettysburg.

statement: The Second Corps marched from Taneytown toward Gettysburg at 1.30 p. m. on 1 July, bivouacked about 3 miles in rear of the town and came up to the field next morning: by the road between Taneytown and Gettysburg, the Taneytown Road.
reasoning: The corps marched from Taneytown toward Gettysburg on 1 July and bivouacked 3 miles in rear of the town; Hazard (R132) prints the artillery brigade, which moved with the corps, on the Taneytown road 3 miles southeast of Gettysburg that night, and Bradley (R094) and Forster (PA2-S015) print the Taneytown road for the infantry of the First Division.

source.author: Maj. Gen. Winfield S. Hancock
source.quote: marched from Taneytown toward Gettysburg at 1..30 p. m.
source.cite: OR Ser. I vol. 27 pt. 1, OR27-1-R076 Maj. Gen. Winfield S. Hancock, p. 369

statement: Caldwell prints that his division arrived on the field on the morning of 2 July and was placed in position by Hancock on the left of the Second Division, in columns of regiments by brigades.

source.author: Brig. Gen. John C. Caldwell
source.quote: My command arrived on the field of battle on the morning of July 2,
source.cite: OR Ser. I vol. 27 pt. 1, OR27-1-R077 Brig. Gen. John C. Caldwell, p. 379

place.printed: on the left of the Second Division

note: The brigades and regiments print their own hours between the dawn march (Brooke, Kelly) and about 10 a. m. (Scherrer, 52d New York; Smith, 69th New York): all carried, none chosen.

statement: Caldwell prints that Hancock placed the division on the left of the Second Division in columns of regiments by brigades, where it stayed until it was sent toward the left in the afternoon.

source.author: Brig. Gen. John C. Caldwell
source.quote: was placed in position by General Hancock on the left of the Second Division,
source.cite: OR Ser. I vol. 27 pt. 1, OR27-1-R077 Brig. Gen. John C. Caldwell, p. 379

place.printed: on the left of the Second Division

note: The ledger holds the sentence without an anchor; the unit anchor makes it placeable relative to the Second Division, whose own place is held by the troop map (TM2-141).

statement: The consolidated field return of 4 July prints for the First Division, present for duty, 152 officers and 1,694 men, 1,846 in all (the return reads the columns of the three divisions in a row).

source.author: Consolidated field return of the Army of the Potomac, July 4, 1863
source.page_basis: scan-leaf map docs/battle-theatre/kit/evidence/or27_leaf_pages.json, part 1, leaf 176, printed page 153 (the running heads inside the table are not all legible)
source.cite: OR Ser. I vol. 27 pt. 1, OR27-1-R008 Consolidated field return of the Army of the Potomac, July 4, 1863, p. 153

note: The OCR prints the three divisions in a row (officers 152, 170, 209; men 1,694, 1,807, 2,422; aggregates 1,846, 1,977, 2,631): the first of each is the First Division. This is the strength of 4 July after the battle, not of 2 July. The kit evidence file holds the same row.
